## 6. `ChartRing` vs `univSeed`'s ring — the probe is **not** decision-grade as written

`IsChartClause` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean:119-127`) quantifies over `U : ∀ i j, DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g`, i.e. over `DivFamZar C (PairChartRing … ⧸ divCarveIdeal … b1 (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j) pi g`.

So the two `RZ`s are the same ring *provided* the transport aligns — the divisor argument to `DivCarveChartRing` is the same `A B` pair in both, and only the basis argument differs by that reindexing.

That alignment is **not proved anywhere in the tree**, and no declaration connects any of the four `divFamZarUniv*` (`…Univ.lean:213`, `…UnivFree.lean:183`, `…UnivAny.lean:261`, `…UnivZarLocal.lean:287`) to `IsChartClause`. Grepped: `IsChartClause` appears only in `DivRepAffPullClause.lean` and `DivRepChartRange.lean` (which states `isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq`, `:186`), never with `univSeed` or `divFamZarUniv`. `DivRepChartClassUniv.lean:67` says so itself: "It produces no certificate, hence no `DivFamZar` over `R_Z` and no `IsChartClause`."

So the answer to the caller's own gating question: `univSeed` is over `DivCarveChartRing … b1 b2 i j`, while U2's `IsChartClause` binds `DivFamZar C (DivCarveChartRing … b1 (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j) pi g`. /-- **Clause (c1)-finite at a piece implies leak-freeness there** — the direction the lane had
assumed since I-0209 without a proof.  With `finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty` it makes
the two conditions equivalent. -/
theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength (j : A.index)
    (h : Module.Finite R (A.colength j)) :
    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
  have hclosed := IsAffineOpen.isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient
    (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces j) (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) h
  rw [Scheme.zeroLocus_span] at hclosed
  have hset : (relCurve C R).zeroLocus {A.eqn j} ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      = (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
        \ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
    ext x
    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Scheme.mem_zeroLocus_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
      forall_eq, Set.mem_sdiff, SetLike.mem_coe]
    exact and_comm
  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_pieces j, ← hset]
  exact hclosed

/-- **Leak-freeness and clause (c1)-finite are the same condition at a piece.** -/
theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength (j : A.index) :
    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ ↔ Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  ⟨A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j, A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength j⟩

meeting both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)`, over any base and after any Zariski shrink. -/
theorem supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified {n : ℕ}
    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
      ∨ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
  A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected hconn
    fun j => A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength j (hc.finite_colength j)

end DivisorAdaptation

9	# DECIDING THE FORK: what non-injectivity of the unrestricted Abel chart actually costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` makes the fork precise and machine-checked:
12	`IsChartLocusFibre` implies the Abel chart is a monomorphism, which three headers
13	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
14	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`) assert it is not.  Exactly one side is right, and
15	the guard leaves the deciding statement — non-injectivity — as prose.
16	
17	**This file reduces that statement to divisor data.**  The reduction is what was missing: the
18	Abel chart's app does not take divisors, it takes `D.left`-points, so "two divisors in one
19	linear system" is not by itself a witness.  Reading `abelChartApp_eq`
20	(`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`), a point `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is sent to the **pair**
21	
22	  `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl))⟩`
23	
24	so a non-injectivity witness owes *two* agreements, not one: the Σ-components `x ≫ D.hom` must
25	agree before the classes are in the same type at all.  That is the trap the c9b row names.
26	
27	## What is proved here
28	
29	The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs, and its converse:
30	
31	* `not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points` — from two `D.left`-points over one test with
32	  **equal structure morphism** and **equal chart value** but distinct as points, the Abel chart
33	  fails to be injective; `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points` composes that with the guard to
34	  refute `IsChartLocusFibre`.
35	* `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar` — the same reduction **reparameterised onto divisor
36	  families**: two distinct elements of `divFamZar C π n T` with equal chart value.  Here the
37	  Σ-component hypothesis is not passed in: both points are `(rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ).left`, whose
38	  structure morphism is the test's own by `Over.w`, so `hstruct` holds by construction.
39	  **This is a change of parameterisation, not a strengthening** — the two forms are
40	  inter-derivable (from the family form, take `T := Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and use
41	  `rep.homEquiv.injective` for distinctness), so `hstruct` is absorbed by the choice of test
42	  rather than eliminated.  Its value is that the family form is the shape a divisor argument
43	  produces, with no scheme-theoretic side condition to discharge first.
44	* `abelChartApp_inj_iff` — the unfolded shape of injectivity at a test, by `Iff.rfl`.  A
45	  documentation lemma only: it has no call site below, and `abelChartApp_eq`
46	  (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`) already exposes both components.
47	
48	## What is NOT proved here, stated so this file is not over-read
49	
50	**Nothing here exhibits a curve on which the hypothesis holds, and no theorem below closes the
51	fork.**  Every statement here is an implication whose antecedent is open.  What remains is
52	exactly:
53	
54	  for some curve, some test `T`, and some `n`: two *distinct* elements of `divFamZar C π n T`
55	  whose `chartValue` agree.
56	
57	Three things to know before pricing that, and the third is the one that moves.
58	
59	1. Over a field test it is the classical `h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≥ 2 ⇒ |D|` has two points.
60	   `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
61	   is the exact boundary: uniqueness holds **at** `h⁰ = 1`, so the hypothesis to arrange is
62	   `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  It is the statement to contradict, not to apply.
63	2. The passage from two *divisors* to two distinct *elements of `divFamZar`* is not free: the
64	   families are a quotient of local-equation data (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`), so distinct
65	   divisors need not give distinct families until that equivalence is read.  Nothing here
66	   assumes otherwise.
67	3. **`n` is not free.**  At `n = g` the chart's own degree calibration makes the *fibrewise*
68	   linear system a single point for free: over a field `K`, an effective `K`-divisor of degree
69	   `g` with `Subsingleton H¹` has `h⁰ = 1` exactly (`degAt_chartTwist`'s `+g` discussion in
70	   `Pic0ChartLocus.lean:178-201`, and the rank anchor
71	   `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`, `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`, giving
72	   `h⁰ = g + (1 − g) = 1`).  So the *fibrewise* form of the headers' reason — a
73	   positive-dimensional `|D|` — is unavailable at `n = g` wherever `H¹` vanishes.
74	
75	**AND HERE IS THE LIMIT OF THAT OBSERVATION, which item 3 must not be read past.**  Every anchor
76	in item 3 is fibrewise over one field: `CurveDivisor` over `K`, `h⁰` a `finrank` over `K`,
77	`degAt` evaluated at `overSpec k K`-points.  The obligation is **general-test**: injectivity of
78	`.app (op Y)` at arbitrary `Y`, and correspondingly distinctness in `divFamZar C π n T` at
79	arbitrary `T`.  A fibrewise anchor does not settle a general-test statement, and the brick that
80	would bridge them is *relative* GAP-2 — exactly `ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor`
81	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`), which `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:160-161` names as
82	"the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2" and which **nothing in the tree produces**: no declaration
83	concludes `s₁ = s₂` for two `divFamZar` sections from an equality of their classes.
84	
85	So item 3 **relocates** the fork; it does not shrink it.  What it changes is what a witness
86	should aim at: a bare "two divisors in one linear system" is the wrong target, because at `n = g`
87	with `h¹ = 0` there are none fibrewise — so a witness wants a point of the divisor scheme where
88	`H¹` fails to vanish, or a genuinely relative failure of uniqueness that no fibre sees.  Which
89	of those two it is, is undecided here.  (The degree-`g`/`h⁰ = 1` link is `ajcr-p4`'s measurement,
90	I-0888; the fibrewise/general-test caveat is a fresh-context review's, I-0923/I-0924.)
91	-/

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
  rfl

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
  rw [← picEtMap_comp]

/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

variable (C) in
/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
points. -/

    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=

/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.

The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism

the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}

    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
